messages:
maria: seeing a flurry of OOMs on hosted-gpu-3 last night tied to long-context chats (>12k tokens). stack traces point at kv-cache page growth and repeated slab allocations. not a simple mem leak, looks like reuse failure + fragmentation
raj: yikes. is this in prod or dedicated?
maria: prod hosted. affected ~8 pods over 2 hours, all on same kernel selection (fp16-quant path). logs attached in the incident thread.
dan: can you paste the small repro log? even a snippet helps.
maria: here —
```
E2026-03-17T22:41:12Z OOM in kv_cache.cpp: allocation failed for slab 4096 at 0x7f...
stack: kv::allocate_slab -> kv::assign_prefix -> runtime::attach_kv -> runtime::dispatch_token
kv_stats: live_pages=18345, free_pages=124, fragmented_slots=27, reuse_attempts=1
```

sophie: reuse_attempts=1 stands out. we usually see ~20. that suggests reuse logic short-circuited. any recent rollouts for compacted-kv reuse?
maria: rolled compacted-reuse v2 last week (kernel selector + reuse optimizer). rollout metric looked fine on perf testbeds but I think it regresses on heavy long-context traffic.
kevin: could kernel selection be influencing layout? fp16-quant path uses different slab size and packing heuristics. if it packs differently fragmentation could spike.
raj: agree. hypothesis: reuse optimizer picks a near-fit slot but kernel packing changed slab alignment causing false mismatches and forced new slabs -> fragmentation -> paging.
dan: actionable: can we toggle compacted-reuse v2 off for hosted for a single ring and see if OOMs stop?
maria: yeah I rolled a canary off last hour in region-us-west-2, numbers dropped for that ring. ops-bot posted the rollout.
deploy-bot: rollback of feature compacted-reuse v2 to ring 'us-west-2-canary' initiated by maria at 2026-03-17T23:05:00Z :white_check_mark:
raj: good. parallel idea: add a soft-evict threshold based on contiguous free pages rather than total free pages. that avoids heavy fragmentation before OOM.
sophie: also we should add a fallback to smaller-kernel path (fp32-quant-slim) when memory pressure surges. it costs latency but avoids downtime.
kevin: batching heuristics might amplify this. large dynamic batches keep KV pinned; we saw high p99 concurrency spikes during the incident. maybe cap dynamic batch size when context > 8k tokens.
maria: noted. I'm sketching a short-term playbook: 1) rollback reuse v2 (done for canary) 2) enable contiguous-free-page threshold 3) cap dynamic batch for longctx 4) add graceful degrade to smaller model variant 5) emit detailed kv reuse telemetry.
raj: for (2) can we implement an immediate guard in runtime to treat fragmented free pages as unusable and trigger compaction or spill-to-disk earlier? cheap heuristic to avoid OOM spiral.
dan: and (5) we need micro-profiling traces: cache allocation timeline per request id, reuse decisions, kernel path selected, and batch size. that will let us correlate kernel selection -> fragmentation.
maria: I'm adding instrumentation tickets. also we observed a perf regression in reuse hotpath: a new inline inlined comparator increased CPU in tight loop causing slower reuse checks -> fewer reuse attempts before allocating new slabs. that explains reuse_attempts=1.
kevin: oh that's a nasty micro-regression. roll that change back in the repo if it's still live.
sophie: operational mitigation: implement circuit breaker that rejects requests above X tokens when free_pages < Y and fragmentation > Z, returning a 503 with a hint to retry smaller context. fewer users will be impacted than OOMing pods.
raj: for long-term: rework packing strategy so kernel selection informs slab alignment. ideally the kernel selector and allocator share a slab-layout contract.
maria: agreed. I'll schedule a design sync with eng-runtime + kernel-selection + eng-ml tomorrow. prepping reproducible load test.
ops-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-0427-kv-oom-longctx. assigned to maria, raj. severity: P2.
dan: approve. also add a synthetic e2e that runs 50k long-context requests/day to catch regressions in CI.
kevin: quick note: we had one model fallback already implemented but it didn't trigger because the fallback condition checked total memory, not fragmentation. update needed.
sophie: I'll file a small PR to change fallback to use contiguous_free_pages metric.
maria: thanks. next steps: patch allocator guard (short-term), telemetry + perf traces (mid), packing contract design (long). I'll post progress in this thread. :v:
